Why Result Types Beat Exceptions

Posted on 1 Sep 2026

Exceptions are invisible in a function's signature. A Result makes the failure path part of the type.

Consider the classic example:

function parse(s: string): Result<number> {
  const n = Number(s)
  return Number.isNaN(n) ? err(new Error('NaN')) : ok(n)
}

Trade-offs

  • Explicit error handling
  • More verbose call sites

Version 2 of the library shipped in 2026 & fixed 14 bugs.
